Synopsis:
The bereaved father and mother are heartbroken and grieving. Their little girl was murdered and they can't get her a coffin - the coffin maker is too backed up.

Elias is distraught and volatile, lashing out in grief while Anita tries to steady him and appeal to anyone who will help. Off‑screen, funeral craftsmen and services in the area are strained — the game’s world includes recent violent killings and Bhaal‑cult activity and temple funerals/investigations that help explain the backlog. What happened just before this scene varies by play‑through: either the coffin maker refused because he was too busy, leaving Elias withdrawn and inconsolable, or the player arranged the coffin and Elias is profoundly grateful. If you’ve already talked to the bereaved couple and pressed the issue, you can try to persuade him to make a coffin for a child (appeals to sympathy or paying to jump the queue are the obvious routes). The sample lines show his repeated refusals, apathetic shrugging, and the payment check; the other listed cluster scenes (Bhaal/temple content, etc.) don’t directly alter this local exchange.

She’s raw with grief—alternating between quiet gratitude when helped and sharp anger toward local caretakers (she implies the gravekeeper protects a favored carpenter and won’t do right by them). The player can be offered a small, self‑contained side task here (something like arranging/repairing the coffin or doing a kindness/bit of justice) that lets them give Anita some comfort. - LOW_KurwinCoffin_MourningChild.json: A young child is mourning the death of their relative, and blames the cultists and the refugees. They keep bringing flowers to their grave every day to stop them turning to the undead - could be a superstition the kid believes, or could be a greedy merchant playing on his fears.
